title: Does Eye Black Actually Work? #Shorts
description:
Does eye black actually work? The idea: sunlight hits your cheekbones and bounces up into your eyes, and that glare washes out the ball against a bright sky. Black grease soaks up that light instead of bouncing it. In 2003, Yale eye doctors tested it in bright sunlight: with the grease, people saw contrast a little better. The anti-glare stickers with logos didn't help at all, scoring the same as a smear of petroleum jelly. Players used to use burnt cork. So yes, it works. A little.

Explained in 60, podcast edition
